remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.0: Searching for how to remove Fireflies AI from Teams usually means one of two situations. Either the bot just showed up in your meeting and you want it gone, or it keeps coming back no matter what you try. Both are covered below, across Microsoft Teams, Zoom and Google Meet.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.1: Usually someone on the invite connected their calendar to Fireflies, and its auto-join setting sent the bot (named Fred) into every meeting. Kicking it out once fixes today. Changing that setting fixes tomorrow.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.2: Each of these 3 ways to remove Fireflies from a live Microsoft Teams meeting takes under 30 seconds:
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.3: Speed matters here. According to Fireflies' help center, removal within the first 3 minutes means no transcript or notes get created ([Fireflies guide](https://guide.fireflies.ai/articles/7098191513-how-to-remove-fireflies-from-a-meeting-or-stop-it-from-joining)).
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.4: Zoom and Google Meet work almost identically, and the steps take about 10 seconds:
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.5: Zoom only lets a host or co-host remove a participant. Google Meet behaves similarly when Host Management is on: hosts and co-hosts alone can remove people.

remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.7: There's also **Recording Rules**, which block meetings by keyword, email address or domain. Because rules override auto-join, you could, say, block every external client meeting in one go.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.8: To remove Fireflies AI from Microsoft Teams permanently, 2 people usually need to act: the person whose account sends the bot must delete their Fireflies account or disconnect it, and a Teams admin should block the app. Do just one? The bot often keeps joining.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.9: Blocking the Fireflies app takes a Teams admin 4 steps in the Teams admin center, per a Microsoft community answer ([Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4429002/removing-fireflies-ai-note-taker-bot-from-microsof)):
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.10: That alone isn't always enough. Users in the same thread report the bot still slipping in, since Fireflies can join as a meeting participant through calendar access. Admins often add 2 more controls:
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.11: Menu names drift over time. Check Microsoft's current documentation for your tenant.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.12: Fireflies is a legitimate, widely used product with HIPAA and SSO on its $39 Enterprise plan. Joining "uninvited" is usually a settings issue. Not a security breach. Once one attendee connects their calendar with auto-join on, Fred shows up to every meeting on that calendar, even ones other people organized.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.13: Still, treat any unexpected recorder as a privacy question: who owns the bot, where does the recording go, and did everyone agree? Several US states require all parties to consent before a call is recorded.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.14: Removing Fireflies because a visible bot bothers clients, or because it crashes too many meetings? Pick a tool with tighter control over when it records.

remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.18: Removing Fireflies from Outlook takes 2 steps: delete `fred@fireflies.ai` from the attendee list of each event, then change auto-join to **Only when I invite** so it stops being added. Want access cut completely? Delete the Fireflies account and strip its permissions from your Microsoft account.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.19: Recurring meetings need the whole series edited, not a single occurrence. Otherwise Fred returns next week.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.20: Delete or disconnect the Fireflies account that sends the bot, remove fred@fireflies.ai from invites, and have a Teams admin block the app in the Teams admin center under Teams apps, then Manage apps. App blocking alone doesn't always work. Calendar access lets the bot keep joining.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.21: Open the participant list, click the menu next to Fireflies and choose Remove from meeting, or type /ff leave in the meeting chat. Act fast: within the first 3 minutes, Fireflies creates no transcript or notes. In Teams, removing a participant requires host or presenter rights.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.22: Someone on the invite connected their calendar to Fireflies with auto-join turned on. Ask the bot's owner to switch auto-join to Only when I invite, or remove fred@fireflies.ai from the invite. With recurring meetings, edit the whole series rather than one occurrence; otherwise Fred will be back the following week.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.23: It depends on the timing. Removed within the first 3 minutes, Fireflies creates no transcript or notes; removed later, the owner may still get notes for the part it recorded. Without attendee agreement, ask the bot's owner to delete those meeting notes.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.24: Partly, yes. You can remove it from meetings you organize and set your lobby so only organizers bypass it, which leaves the bot waiting outside for the organizer to simply deny it entry each time. Company-wide blocking, though, still requires a Teams admin.
remove-fireflies-ai-from-teams.25: Fireflies is a legitimate product with enterprise security options, including HIPAA and SSO on its Enterprise plan. The usual complaint is uninvited joining via auto-join, and settings control that. Ask who owns the bot and where the recording goes, since several US states require all parties to consent to recording.
